newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: IBM Korea, LG formally announce computer venture.
newsitem.headline: IBM Korea, LG formally announce computer venture.

text.p: IBM Korea and LG Electronics on Tuesday formally announced a joint venture to produce personal computers and parts in a tie-up they hope will dominate the South Korean market.
LG-IBM PC Co will manufacture and market notebook PCs, desk-top PCs, PC servers and computer peripherial devices.

It will be capitalised at $30 million and be 51 percent owned by IBM Korea, a wholly owned unit of U.S. International Business Machines Corp. The rest will be owned by LG Electronics, a unit of LG Group.
"Jointly made products will make their introduction in November this year," Robert Stephenson, the president of IBM Personal System Group, told a news conference.
PC servers and mobile computers would debut first.
"LG-IBM expects annual production of 400,000 to 500,000 units of PCs," said Lee Eun-jun, vice president of LG Electronics. "But it could change depending on domestic demand."
Total sales of PCs in South Korea this year are forecast at two million units, up from 1.64 million last year, according to Dongbang Peregrine Securities.

Lee said the joint venture would utilise LG's existing production lines and there were no plans to add new lines. "We may produce PCs overseas in the future by using our lines abroad or IBM's, but it hasn't been decided yet."
The partners will merge their domestic operations in the joint venture and output will be sold under the LG-IBM brand name for the domestic market and export.

"The focus will be on the Korean market because of its huge potential," said John Koo, the president of LG Electronics. "When we export, the jointly made products will be sold through IBM's sales network."
LG would continue to produce its own brand name products for export.
Koo said LG-IBM brand products would be marketed through LG and IBM Korea's sales channels.

"A combination of IBM's technical strengths in notebook PC and PC server field and LG's strength in multimedia PC, desktop PC and PC network will create the most competitive PC producer in the world," he said.
LG Electronics is South Korea's number three PC maker behind Samsung Electronics and Trigem Computer.
"We aim to become the number one PC maker in the domestic market," said Oh Chang-kyoo, general mananger of IBM Korea, who was appointed chief executive officer of LG-IBM.
"IBM's sales in Korea have been less than what we had expected," said Oh. "But through this joint venture, I believe our PC business will grow and improve."
Samsung has a 30 percent share of the domestic PC market followed by Trigem with 15 percent, according to figures from Hanuri Salomon Securities.
LG Electronics claims a 10-14 percent market share with sales of 160,000 PCs in the first eight months of this year, up sharply from 100,000 units a year earlier.
